notes: kb/Work PB1086/PB2104: Rule (cite.py --check 11.6.4 OK, GR 1): 'Interface-name-1 names the interface declared by this interface definition. However, literal-1, if specified, is the name of the interface that is externalized to the operating environment.' Half 1: OoClassTable.Build registers the interface under interfaceName(0) and every reference resolves through OoNameResolution (the declared word). Half 2: literal-1 is screened by ExternalizedName.Screen (11.6.3 SR1, COBOL1794), stored as OoInterfaceSymbol.ExternalizedName, and is the interface's identity in the external repository (identity = literal-1 ?? word, DESIGN-external-repository 10.6): the compiled assembly's repository record publishes the interface under it, and a separately compiled program reaches it by that name alone. Witness pb2104_import_interface_and_property: the library declares INTERFACE-ID. P2104ISPK AS "P2104-Speaker"; the program is a different compilation group, names it INTERFACE SP AS "P2104-Speaker" (the word P2104ISPK never appears in it), holds an imported class's object and its own class's object in an OBJECT REFERENCE SP, and INVOKE S "SPEAK" prints WOOF / MEOW. Within the group pb974_repository_as_phrase pins the AS match (12.3.8.4 GR2). The emitted CLR interface name is the sanitized declared word (the spec does not fix how an externalized name maps onto host metadata); what is externalized is the record's name. The earlier refutation (nothing externalized under literal-1; no external repository) no longer holds. Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO facility, introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; interface definitions are rejected COBOL0900 at 85). retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Oo/OoInterfaceSymbol.cs#ExternalizedName (the file moved to Binding/Model with the OO symbols' closure (kb/Work PB2402); the same member, re-sited at its new path)
